hints: Differentiate the composite function $(\tan\theta)^2$ using the chain rule.
Use $\sec^2\theta=1/\cos^2\theta$ to put the derivative in the displayed form.
Separate the differential equation into $x\,dx$ and a function of $\theta\,d\theta$.
After dividing by $\cos^2\theta$, split the right side into $\frac{2\tan\theta}{\cos^2\theta}+\sec^2\theta$ and integrate using part (i).
Use $x=1$ at $\theta=\pi/4$ to fix the constant in the integrated relation.
Then set $\theta=\pi/3$ and choose the positive square root because $x>0$.
walkthrough:
Apply the result from part (i) $\int \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{\cos^2\theta}\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \tan^2\theta$ and the standard integral $\int \sec^2\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \tan\theta$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}x^2 = \tan^2\theta + \tan\theta + C$$

Determine the constant of integration $C$ using $x = 1$ when $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:
$$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$$
$$\dfrac{1}{2}(1)^2 = 1^2 + 1 + C$$
$$\dfrac{1}{2} = 2 + C \implies C = \dfrac{1}{2} - 2 = -\dfrac{3}{2}$$

Since $x > 0$, take the positive square root:
$$x = \sqrt{6.4641016} \approx 2.54246$$
